newsitem.title: UK: London freight index collapse seen as no surprise.
newsitem.headline: London freight index collapse seen as no surprise.

text.p: In current conditions it came as no surprise to the dry cargo freight market when the BFI, down 4 today to 997 on Monday, fell below the 1,000 level for the first time since Aug 4, 1987.
A measure of the sharpness of the decline can be estimated from the fact that a year ago the index was at 1,979 and 18 months ago at 2,294.

The malaise for shipowners is apparent in nearly all aspects of the tramp market, not simply BFI tonnage and routes. In addition few brokers profess any optimism about short-term rate prospects, at least not before the arrival of the new North American grain crop towards the end of October.

In a generally quiet market private fixtures were believed to have been concluded by Cargill of 55,000 wheat St Lawrence/Egypt for Oct 5/10, possibly for as little as $8.25, and Geepee may have taken a Panamax delivery U.S. Gulf end Sept for a trip to S.E. Asia.
Cargill quoted fresh enquiries of 55,000 HSS U.S. Gulf/Barcelona-Hamburg range for Oct 4/11 and a caper of 4-5.3 milliion CFT grain Plate and Brazil to the continent for Oct 20/30.
Geepee quoted a new Panamax order delivery U.S. Gulf Oct 20/25 trip Arabian Gulf. Grain houses have very little business on their books.
Reports circulated that China Steel had fixed U Ming caper tonnage with iron ore from West Australia to Kaohsing for end Oct at under $3.50.
These charterers now quote 121,000/10 coal Port Kema/Kaohsiung for Oct 20/30.

Preag also had fresh coal business - 100,000 tonnes Richards Bay/Ensted for Nov 20/30 and Margem was looking for a caper for 120-130,000/10 coal from Hay Point or Roberts Bank to Turkey for Nov 15/30.
Cargill fixed a Panamax with coal from Maracaibo to Ijmuiden on private terms. Guinomar was rumoured to have fixed an over-age 70,000 dwt vessel in the Atlantic for 3-5 months at about $5,500 daily.
Handy-sizes rates for craned bulkers on the continent or trips to the east continue to weaken.
Pan Ocean has taken Aditja Gopal 43,815 dwt delivery Skaw early Oct at $11,000 daily, the sister vessel having previously obtained $11,750 daily in the middle of the month.

LD-Seals was said to have booked a 38,000 dwt vessel for similar business at about $10,500 daily and Pan Ocean has been linked with Dong Fang Hai 37,636 dwt continent/Far East at close to $10,000 daily.

Owners have fared no better in the east where Showa is believed to have continued Bohinj 34,942 dwt for another Nopac/Japan grain sailing and the western bulk-relet Multipurpose 3 41,455 dwt Australia/Japan both at more economical rates than last done.
